previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with shortness of breath, painless hematuria, and right upper quadrant pain. He was found to have multifocal pneumonia and a small right pleural effusion, likely contributing to his dyspnea. Given his recent hospitalization and toxic appearance, he was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, later de-escalated to oral Augmentin and doxycycline after a negative MRSA screen. He also had an acute COPD exacerbation managed with a short course of prednisone and nebulized treatments. His heart failure was acutely decompensated, with elevated BNP; he responded well to IV diuresis and was transitioned back to oral torsemide. His supratherapeutic INR was managed by holding warfarin temporarily and resuming at discharge with an INR of 2.0. Hematuria was attributed to chronic nephrolithiasis and anticoagulation, with urology follow-up recommended. He improved clinically and was discharged home with service, on a 10-day antibiotic course, fluid and sodium restrictions, and multiple outpatient follow-ups.
